verdict.tagline: Clunky physics hiding a genuinely hilarious cooperative sandbox experience.
for_you_if: you want endless community workshop levels
you play with friends who laugh at clumsy movement
you can master awkward physics puzzles
not_for_you_if: you need reliable online multiplayer connections
you expect crossplay between different platforms

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the controls and climbing mechanics as janky, difficult to get used to, and frustrating at times.

citations.review_text: It is a good physics puzzle game after you get used to the controls. There are too many achievements to possibly get in one playthrough and I love it.

From the era of janky physics-based indie games, we got this gem.  Among all the others, it has stood the test of time, and I'd still recommend it today.  The controls are terrible, but the rules are consistent.  Once you get them, you just kind of have them.  The movement never really stops being janky, especially some of the more precise object interactions.  But after a while, it fades into the background and becomes part of the charm.

In hindsight, not only is the first level a tutorial, but the next several levels are as well.  The game gradually introduces new mechanics before the later half of the campaign - and the plethora of bonus levels - starts combining them into larger, more curated environments.  Supposedly, every puzzle can be completed solo [i](and without the advanced wall-climbing exploits that I could never learn)[/i], though I certainly wouldn't want to.  Like almost every other game in existence, this is not only faster but significantly better with one to three friends.

They keep adding new maps and, therefore, new achievements.  This is the bane of completionists everywhere.  Be that as it may, when I look at the numbers, I realize I've spent far more time completing far worse games.  So I'm grateful for the long-term support and the sheer amount of content available at this point.  I'm mostly left wondering when [b]Human: Fall Flat 2[/b] will arrive and what exactly it could add beyond simply giving us more maps.

While i play this game on occasion it's climbing mechanincs can be downright INFURIATING AT TIMES. Definitely a good game for people who think that Getting over it with Bennet Foddy is a relaxing experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as featuring physics-based movement with a floppy, unpredictable character, which makes climbing, grabbing, swinging, and balancing challenging.

citations.review_text:
Funny, and whilst challenging the player to control a floppy "Human", also builds on the players mind.

-An 11 year old kid.

[h1]Human: Fall Flat[/h1]

[b]Human: Fall Flat[/b] is a quirky physics-based puzzle platformer where you control a wobbly, customizable human through surreal, dreamlike levels. The goal? Solve puzzles, explore, and figure out how to get from point A to point B without falling flat… too many times. (store.steampowered.com
)

The game’s core charm is in its physics-based movement. Your character is floppy and unpredictable, which makes even simple tasks hilariously challenging. Climbing, grabbing, swinging, and balancing are all done in a way that feels both clumsy and satisfying — expect lots of accidental falls and funny failures.

[b]Co-op multiplayer[/b] is where it really shines. Up to 8 players can collaborate or unintentionally sabotage each other while trying to solve puzzles. Nothing beats the laughter from watching a friend swing off a ledge or drop a key at the worst possible moment.

[b]What’s good:[/b]
• Physics-based mechanics lead to endless funny moments and creative solutions.
• Levels are colorful, varied, and filled with environmental puzzles.
• Co-op gameplay adds tons of replay value.
• Easy to pick up, no complicated controls or rules.

[b]Some negatives:[/b]
• Solo play can feel a little tedious, especially on tricky puzzles.
• Physics sometimes misbehaves, which can be frustrating.
• Levels are fairly short and may feel repetitive after many runs.
• Not much of a story — it’s mostly about puzzles and chaos.

[u]Overall:[/u]
A lighthearted, silly, and sometimes chaotic puzzle game that’s best enjoyed with friends. The combination of wobbly physics and cooperative play makes every session unpredictable and hilarious.

[b]Final verdict:[/b]
A charming and goofy physics playground that’s easy to jump into, full of laughs, and endlessly replayable in multiplayer. Perfect for casual gaming and funny moments with friends.

[spoiler]Pro tip: Always expect to fall flat… it’s half the fun![/spoiler]
